payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into how embeddings are evaluated against human judgments, particularly focusing on the correlation between model outputs and human similarity assessments.

claims.text: Word-based embedding models generally correlate better with human judgments than character-based models, especially for morphologically simple words.
Character-level models can still perform reasonably well on datasets with out-of-vocabulary words, indicating their competitive nature in evaluation against human judgments.
Incorporating morphology into character-level models improves their performance in producing embeddings that correlate with human judgments.
